title: Application-level ingress/egress firewall matrix + Terraform module contracts
body:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc defines an application-scoped firewall policy matrix and the Terraform module contracts we want teams to consume for private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. The goal is to have a small, composable TF surface that
can express per-app ingress and egress intent, integrate with existing SNAT pools / NAT gateways, and generate auditable firewall rules and network-policy objects.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Clusters use Calico for network-policy enforcement where available; fallback to iptables-based host rules in air-gapped on-prem installs.
- Most customer apps run behind a LB (L4 or L7). Some legacy customers still require hostPort or nodePort exposure.
- NAT behavior matters: many customers use shared SNAT pools; ephemeral port exhaustion is a risk for high-concurrency inference tenants.
- TLS termination choices: TLS at edge (LB) is preferred; some regulated installs require mTLS passthrough to pods.

High-level design goals:
1) Express per-application allowed ingress sources and allowed egress destinations (FQDNs/IP ranges) in a single TF module call.
2) Keep rule explosion manageable: enable wildcards at app-group level, but default to least privilege.
3) Ensure policy ID metadata maps back to product/customer and rollout ticket for traceability.
4) Provide verification tests (curl, dig, tcpdump) and SLO/metric guards for rollout.

Validation matrix (example lines you can paste into spreadsheets):
APP_ID | ALLOWED_INGRESS | ALLOWED_INGRESS_PORTS | ALLOWED_EGRESS_FQDNS | EGRESS_PORTS | NAT_BEHAVIOR | ROLLOUT_STRATEGY | VERIFY_CMD
payments-service | internal-loadbalancer, ops-ip-range | 443, 9411 | vault.redwood.corp, billing.svc.cluster | 443, 8200 | shared-snat:preserve-ports | canary-10% -> 25% | curl -sS --resolve billing.svc.cluster:443:10.0.5.7 https://billing.svc.cluster/health
inference-worker | internal-lb, admin-vpn | 50051, 22 | model-registry.storage, metrics.ingest | 50051, 443 | dedicated-snat-pool:port-preserving | staged-pin -> full | nc -vz model-registry.storage 443; dig +short model-registry.storage
batch-ingest | ops-subnet | 8080 | object-store.company.net | 443, 9200 | shared-snat:port-rewrite | immediate | curl -I https://object-store.company.net/v1/ping

Terraform module contract (proposal):
Module name: redwood/app_firewall (registry internal)
- Inputs (short names; add tags/labels for audit):
  - app_id (string) : unique id for mapping to product/customer (required)
  - environment (string) : prod|staging|dev (default prod)
  - ingress_groups (list of objects as string-encoded JSON allowed in some consumers) : high-level source groups (examples: internal-lb, admin-vpn, ops-ip-range)
  - ingress_ports (list of number) : allowed inbound port set
  - egress_targets (list of strings) : fqdn or cidr or tag (e.g. vault.redwood.corp, 10.2.0.0/16)
  - egress_ports (list of number)
  - nat_profile (string) : shared-snat|dedicated-snat|none; additional flags: port-preserve, port-rewrite
  - policy_tier (string) : default|strict|audit (default default)
  - labels (map string->string) : product, owner, ticket_id
  - enable_calico (bool) : if true generate NetworkPolicy; else generate host firewall rules (default true)
  - mtu_workaround (bool) : optional, for on-prem links with overhead
- Outputs:
  - policy_id (string) : stable id for lookup in console and audit logs
  - applied_resources (list of strings) : names/ids of created k8s/network resources
  - tf_state_notes (string) : human-text summary for ops runbook

Implementation notes and anti-patterns:
- Avoid generating per-pod iptables rules. The module should generate set-based policies (selectors) to keep etags small and reconciliation fast.
- For egress FQDNs, prefer a sidecar egress-agent that translates FQDNs into CIDRs at plan time for on-prem; for cloud installs we can rely on cloud-managed resolver groups.
- Do not rely on DNS TTL for security: always treat FQDN->CIDR mapping as advisory and surface a reconciliation job to refresh CIDRs periodically.
- When nat_profile=shared-snat, expose a knob to request a soft-cap on concurrent connections; expose alert thresholds so platform SRE can shard SNAT pools proactively.

Upgrade and rollout plan (per-customer):
1) Plan (working day): generate policy in dry-run mode, collect warmed-up egress CIDRs, list affected apps and owners.
2) Canary (0-10% traffic): apply new policy in audit mode (Calico log-only) or apply host-rules in allow-with-logging. Watch for denied flows.
3) Incremental (10-50%): promote to enforce for low-risk ports, keep audit for sensitive egress (billing, vault).
4) Full migration: flip policy_tier to strict and remove old host firewall rules. Keep a 48–72 hour post-mortem window.
5) Rollback: terraform apply using previous policy_id (modules should support versioned policy_id). Immediately revert to prior NAT profile if port exhaustion observed.

Validation and operational checks (copyable commands):
- Verify ingress path from a given source IP: curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null --connect-timeout 5 https://<app-host>:<port>/health
- DNS->CIDR check (on controlplane node): dig +short +nocmd example.remote.service | xargs -n1 -I{} whois {} || traceroute {}
- Conntrack usage: sudo cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l (watch baseline before rollout)
- SNAT pool saturation (cloud): cloudcli nat describe --id <nat-id> --metric port_usage
- Tcpdump on host-facing interface (for edge troubleshooting): sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host <source-ip> and port <port> -c 200 -nn

Acceptance / unit tests for TF module (CI suggestions):
- Plan-only test: module plan contains expected tags/labels matching app_id and ticket_id
- Dry-run calico policy diff: use calicoctl to validate networkpolicy selectors resolve to expected pod sets
- E2E smoke: spin small test app and assert that disallowed egress is blocked (curl to blocked FQDN times out) and allowed egress succeeds
- IP exhaustion test: simulated concurrent connections to a public endpoint using hey orwrk to validate connection counts and port reuse behavior

Monitoring & alerts to add before enforcing policy:
- increase in "calico_dropped_packets_total" -> alert at 1% above baseline per app
- conntrack table usage > 60% -> paging to SRE
- SNAT port utilization > 75% -> warn and trigger sharding workflow
- DNS resolution failures for mapped FQDNs > 1% over 5m -> raise and fallback to cached CIDRs

Open questions for engineering tradeoffs (to discuss in sync):
- Do we prefer translation-of-FQDN-to-CIDR at plan time (faster rules) or a runtime egress-agent (more accurate but heavier)?
- For on-prem: host firewall vs Calico; what's the fallback when Calico isn't present or is restricted by policy?
- Is port-preserving NAT non-negotiable for high-concurrency inference tenants? Can we provide session affinity instead?

Next actions (owners):
- Marcus: draft initial TF module scaffold and basic CI tests (owner) -> target PR by 2024-11-20
- Ava: run an inventory of apps that will need dedicated-snat and list top 10 by concurrency -> due 2024-10-04 (in progress)
- Ravi: prototype a FQDN->CIDR reconciliation job for on-prem and test on staging -> prototype by 2024-11-01
- Lina: add monitoring dashboards for SNAT and conntrack usage and wire alerts -> ETA 2024-10-15

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a working draft; prefer short, actionable inputs on the TF contract shape and the must-have verification steps. Avoid bikeshedding naming; focus on safety for high-throughput inference workloads.
- If you have a customer case where we MUST allow ephemeral outbound port rewriting, call it out with an example (app_id + peak-concurrency).

Revision history:
- 2024-09-18 initial draft by Marcus
- 2024-10-02 added validation matrix examples and upgrade steps (Ava)
- 2024-11-07 expanded TF contract outputs and CI checklist (Ravi)
